name: 观水法 Guanshuifa
line: Modelled from plate 16 of 1783-86, Ohlmer's photograph of 1873 and the photographs since 1914 (the panels re-erected in 1977, the platform in place), the plan S01 and Durand's survey (S603); every figure is a reading (C) unless the row says otherwise. Faces no picture shows (the screen's brick back, the wall's south face) are carried round (assumed).
rows: five carved marble panels of European arms in a concave screen 14.4 m over its end piers (P0343, S01, C), its ends 2.8 m forward (P0640, P0764, C); the socle 1.3 m (S603, B), panels 2.2 m high (P0764, C), cornice 6.3 m above the court, a crest and eight urns (plate 16, C); brick backing behind (S02, B; its depth assumed). The panels were set back in 1977 on their old spot (S817, B)
the round platform 0.7 m above the court with 5 convex steps (P0344, P0764; in place, S603 p.129, B); on it the throne with its canopy, 3 m high, and the low balustrade with trophies (plate 16, C)
two trophy pedestals before the end piers and two obelisks on their bases beyond them, their balls 4.4 m above the court (plate 16; the obelisks stand today, P0764, C)

the side gates 33.8 m apart (S01, C) on the gardens' level, 1.3 m above the court (S603, B), each with a flight of 10 steps down (plate 16, C) and the form of P0193; clipped hedges and the plain back wall (plate 16, C)
white marble (S02 pp.158-159, B), the backing and the wall rendered brick, the throne gilt (C: the plate is not coloured)
